history.period: Ancient (2nd century CE per some sources; 6th century Chand-era per others)
history.summary: Hilltop Shakti temple at Kasar Devi village, about 8 km from Almora on the Almora-Bageshwar road. DATE CONFLICT: sources variously claim a 2nd-century origin and a 6th-century Chand-dynasty construction (verify). Swami Vivekananda meditated here in the 1890s; the adjacent Crank's Ridge (Hippie Hill) drew counterculture seekers in the 1960s-70s. The popular claim that the site sits on the Van Allen radiation belt is folklore, not science (no NASA study supports it). CSV town/state correction: CSV says town 'Almora Cantonment' and holds town names in the state column; actual town is Almora (Kasar Devi village) and the state is Uttarakhand. Opening-hour claims conflict across sources (6 AM-6 PM, 5 AM-7 PM, 6 AM-7 PM, 7 AM-7 PM); verify locally.

name: Kasar Devi Temple
town_description: Almora is a historic hill town in Kumaon, Uttarakhand, perched on a ridge of the Kumaon Hills at about 1,638 m. A former Chand-dynasty capital, it is known for its temples, bazaars, and panoramic Himalayan views.

travel.road: About 8 km from Almora town on the Almora-Bageshwar highway; reachable by taxi/auto-rickshaw from Almora

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (clear skies); also pleasant October to June
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported variously as 6:00 AM-6:00 PM, 5:00 AM-7:00 PM, 6:00 AM-7:00 PM and 7:00 AM-7:00 PM across sources - verify locally
